'''Sergey Vyacheslavovich Savelyev''' ({{langx|ru|Серге́й Вячесла́вович Саве́льев}}; born March 7, 1959)<ref>[http://poznavatelnoe.tv/savelev Сергей Савельев | Познавательное ТВ]</ref> is a Russian doctor of biological sciences, Professor.<ref>{{cite web|title=Состав диссертационного совета|url=http://morfolhum.ru/dissovet/sostav-dissertacionnogo-soveta/|website=morfolhum.ru|accessdate=2020-08-25|language=ru}}</ref> Sergey Savelyev's statements and books have been repeatedly criticized by experts for a large number of factual errors and incorrect conclusions.<ref name="хх2" >{{cite web|author=Алексей Малов|title=Объявлены 10 номинантов на антипремию "Почётный Академик ВРАЛ" — за вклад в лженауку|url=https://22century.ru/allsorts/69690|publisher=хх2 век|date=8 September 2018|accessdate=2021-06-29|language=ru}}</ref>

==Biography==

Born in Moscow, he graduated from the Biology and Chemistry Faculty of MGZPI (now the [[Sholokhov Moscow State University for Humanities]]), worked at the Brain Institute of the [[USSR Academy of Medical Sciences]], since 1984 at the Institute of Human Morphology RAMS. The author of the idea of cerebral sorting.

==Scientific activity==
For many years engaged in the study of fetal pathologies of the nervous system, he develops methods of their diagnosis{{Citation needed|date=November 2021|reason=}}.

In 2002 he published a monograph, illustrating it with original snapshots of entire human embryos in the first days after implantation and neurulation period{{Citation needed|date=November 2021|reason=He usually doesn't publish research photos.}}.

For many years he is engaged in research in the field of paleoneurology with the Paleontological Institute of Russian Academy of Sciences.
Together with senior scientists of the Institute A.V. Lavrov (laboratory of mammals) and V.R.  Alifanov (laboratory of paleoherpetology) he established the principles of brain organization of dinosaurs, creodonts and gienodonts{{Citation needed|date=November 2021|reason=}}.

In 2013 he headed the working group to study the brain of a mammoth, which included employees of the Research Institute of Human Morphology RAMS, Yakutsk Academy of Sciences and the Paleontological Institute RAS.<ref>{{cite web |last1=жизнь |first1=Редакция журнала Наука и |title=Российские учёные впервые в мире начали исследование мозга мамонта |url=http://www.nkj.ru/news/21991/ |website=www.nkj.ru |date=10 April 2013 |language=ru}}</ref>

In 2014, he led the experiment "Gecko-F4", the purpose of which was to study the effect of microgravity on the sexual behavior, the body of adult animals and the embryonic development of geckos Phelsuma ornata in a two-month orbital experiment on the Russian research satellite "[[Foton-M No.4]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.militarynews.ru/story.asp?rid=1&nid=351161|title=Интерфакс-Агентство Военных Новостей|publisher=www.militarynews.ru|accessdate=2016-10-04}}</ref>

Sergey Savelyev is the author of the idea of cerebral sorting.

==Critics==
Russian paleontologist [[Stanislav Drobyshevsky]] and science journalist Sergey Sokolov published very detailed and devastated critics on the Saveljev´s book "Возникновение мозга человека" (Human brain genesis).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://antropogenez.ru/review/686/|title=Рецензия на книгу "Возникновение мозга человека" на сайте "Антропогенез.ру"}}</ref> 
In 2018 Saveliev got the award "Почетный академик ВРАЛ" (rough translation would be 'Honorable member of academy LIED',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjlIXha0zhU|title=Видео премии 2018 года|website=[[YouTube]] }}</ref> an award, mocking pseudo-scientific research).
